questions.question: In QrScanFab/Layout.tsx, is every load-bearing check live rather than a placeholder — does the onScan handler call the real, imported resolveScanDestination export (not a local stub that always returns null or always returns a fixed destination); is canUseCameraQrScanner() the actual guard evaluated at render/tap time (not a frozen true/false constant); does the FAB's visibility genuinely read the shared hideBottomNav predicate (not a hardcoded display value that happens to match current routes); and are the new 'scanner' i18n strings real EN/DE copy rather than TODO/placeholder text?

Does the Navigation UI module (Layout.tsx / QrScanFab.tsx) respect architecture.md's Boundary Rules — consuming resolveScanDestination as a pure string->string|null function without re-implementing any card/invite parsing itself, consuming NpubQrScanner only through its existing onScan(payload) string contract without editing the group component's internal decode/camera logic, and never adding the FAB to navItems (the shared array driving both the bottom bar and the hamburger overlay)?

Could Navigation UI be deleted and rewritten without modifying any file outside its dependencies_allowed list? If not, which cross-module dependencies exist and do they flow through declared seam contracts in architecture.md?

Do app/tests/unit/scannerCopy.i18n.test.ts and app/tests/e2e/mobile-qr-scanner-fab.spec.ts together give real coverage of the FAB's rendering, gating, and scan-routing behavior — following the repo's no-jsdom/no-renderHook convention (pure-function extraction for logic, Playwright for DOM-level assertions) — and are the onScan-routing tests exercising resolveScanDestination for real (per S1's export) rather than a mock-spy that always returns a canned value, so a regression in S1's routing logic would actually be caught by S2's tests?

Does the shipped behavior match the epic's design decisions as a whole — DD1 (navigate straight to the resolved destination, no intermediate in-scanner confirmation step), DD4 (the FAB is its own fixed, centered, elevated element bypassing navItems entirely, not a slot added to the existing bottom-bar item list), and DD6 (an unrecognised value shows the unrecognised-link message and the scanner keeps scanning rather than closing or erroring)?

Does the scan-to-navigate flow uphold the project's privacy invariant (CLAUDE.md) and reject-safely on untrusted decoded content — no relay publish or kind-0/profile broadcast triggered anywhere in the FAB-open-to-navigate path; on an unrecognised/rejected scan, is the raw decoded string never rendered, logged, or persisted (only a generic unrecognised-link message shown); and on camera-permission-denied or camera-unavailable, is no camera stream data or raw decode content exposed in the fallback UI?

Does the scanner FAB render only at the mobile breakpoint (Chakra display base visible, md hidden), matching the pattern of every other mobile-only surface in Layout.tsx, and never render at a desktop viewport? Show the production JSX prop and an e2e/unit assertion exercising both a mobile and a desktop viewport, not just a snapshot at one width.

Is the FAB horizontally centered at the bottom of the viewport, positioned with a z-index above the bottom tab bar's zIndex 10, and does it honor env(safe-area-inset-bottom)? Show the actual CSS/style props and confirm via test or documented manual check that the FAB visually sits above (not behind) the bottom bar.

Is the FAB absent from the hamburger overlay and confirmed to not be a member of navItems (the hamburger menu's item set is provably unchanged by this epic)? Show a diff or test asserting navItems' length/contents are unchanged and that the hamburger overlay's rendered item list does not include the FAB.

Does the FAB reuse the exact same hideBottomNav (or equivalent route-visibility) predicate the bottom tab bar already uses, so it is hidden on /contacts and /groups routes carrying a non-empty id query — the same routes that hide the bottom bar? Show the shared predicate being called (not a re-implemented copy) and a test exercising both an open-chat route (hidden) and a non-chat route (visible).

Does tapping the FAB open the camera scanner guarded by canUseCameraQrScanner(), surfacing the unavailable message (not a broken camera view) when that guard is false, and surfacing a distinct permission-denied message on a camera-permission denial? Show both code paths and tests exercising canUseCameraQrScanner() === false and a simulated permission-denial, asserting the two messages are distinct and neither leaves a blank/broken view.

On decoding a valid few.chat card QR, does the app router.push to the card destination (/add#c=…) and close the scanner; on decoding a valid group invite QR, does it router.push to /groups?join=…&admin=…&name=… and close the scanner? Show the onScan handler's branch calling resolveScanDestination and router.push, and a test for each of the two destination kinds asserting both the navigation target and that the scanner UI closes.

On decoding a value resolveScanDestination rejects (returns null), does the app show the unrecognised-link message, refrain from navigating, refrain from surfacing the raw scanned content anywhere in the DOM, and keep the scanner running (not close it)? Show the null-branch handling code and a test asserting router.push was not called, the raw string is absent from rendered output, and the scanner remains active/listening afterward.

Are all scanner-facing strings (FAB aria-label, scanner title/hint, starting-camera, permission-denied, unavailable, unrecognised-link) defined under a dedicated scanner i18n namespace with both en and de entries, consumed exclusively via useCopy() with zero hardcoded user-visible strings in QrScanFab.tsx/the scanner wrapper? Show the i18n.ts namespace entries for both languages and the component call sites, and confirm scannerCopy.i18n.test.ts asserts exact string presence for both locales (following the addContactByNpub.i18n.test.ts precedent).

Does the feature perform zero relay publishes and broadcast zero profile metadata across the entire FAB-tap-to-navigate flow — QR decoding happens purely locally (camera -> qr-scanner, in-page), and navigation to /add or /groups triggers only the pre-existing, already-audited inbound flows with no new kind-0 or other relay-write call introduced by this story? Show a structural trace (call graph or grep across the new/changed files) confirming no relay-publish/NDK-publish call exists in the new code, since this is a negative/structural assertion that cannot be proven by a single example test alone.

The implementation edits app/src/components/groups/NpubQrScanner.tsx (a file NOT listed in S2's stories.json scope.includes) to add two optional props, `onRawScan?: (raw: string) => boolean` and `startingMessage?: string`, because the pre-existing `onScan`/`normaliseScanPayload` gate structurally rejects every group-invite URL before `onScan` ever fires (parseContactCard has no branch for a `/groups/` URL), making AC-SCAN-2's group-invite routing unreachable if NpubQrScanner were reused completely unmodified. Verify: (a) both new props are genuinely optional with the exact pre-existing behavior preserved byte-for-byte when omitted — check NpubQrModal.tsx's two production render sites (ShareContactCard.tsx, pages/settings.tsx) still pass only `mode='display'` and are unaffected; (b) the onRawScan branch correctly short-circuits BEFORE normaliseScanPayload runs, and correctly gates `handledRef`/`scanner.stop()` on the boolean return; (c) this is the only cross-scope-boundary file touched, and no other file outside stories.json's scope.includes for S2 was modified.

During implementation, an in-page probe against this repo's actual Playwright config (chromium launched with `--use-fake-device-for-media-stream --use-fake-ui-for-media-stream`, shared with the calls e2e suite) showed `canUseCameraQrScanner()` evaluates true and `getUserMedia({video:true})` succeeds under a fake `videoinput` device — meaning the camera-unavailable and permission-denied branches of AC-SCAN-1 are structurally UNREACHABLE in this project's e2e harness (the fake device always 'has a camera' and the fake UI flag auto-grants permission). `mobile-qr-scanner-fab.spec.ts` was written to assert only the reachable positive half (scanner opens, real translated title/hint render, no error alert, video element visible) rather than the unavailable-message path the original story brief assumed. Verify: (a) this finding is accurate — re-run or re-derive it independently rather than trusting the claim at face value; (b) the negative branches (unavailableMessage/permissionDeniedMessage props, the try/catch in NpubQrScanner's startScanner) are still structurally correct by code reading even though no automated test exercises them in this repo's current e2e config; (c) whether this is worth a `base:learnings` entry or a BACKLOG finding so a future story doesn't re-discover it from scratch (e.g. a future story needing to actually test the unavailable/permission-denied UI would need either a Playwright project override without the fake-device args, or a manual QA step).

Because the real camera decode path cannot be driven in Playwright (MV-1, manual-only) and unit tests cannot render QrScanFab (no-jsdom convention), the onRawScan -> resolveScanDestination -> router.push wiring in QrScanFab.tsx has NO test coverage exercising it end-to-end with a real decoded value — coverage rests entirely on (a) S1's qr-scan-destination.test.ts unit-testing resolveScanDestination itself in isolation, and (b) code reading of QrScanFab.handleRawScan's plain call-through. Verify by direct code reading that handleRawScan's branching (destination truthy -> setIsOpen(false) + router.push(destination); destination null -> setRejected(true), scanner keeps running) exactly matches AC-SCAN-2/AC-SCAN-3's required behavior, since this is the one load-bearing path in the whole story with no automated end-to-end proof.

Running the full non-relay fast e2e bucket (`make test-e2e-fast`, 71 tests including the new 4) turned up one PRE-EXISTING failure unrelated to this story: `update-detection.spec.ts:70` ('banner is non-blocking — user can still interact with the app') fails on a Playwright strict-mode violation — `page.locator('nav')` resolves to 2 elements (the header nav and the mobile bottom tab bar's `<Box as="nav" data-testid="mobile-bottom-nav">`, both already present in HEAD before this story's changes, from the prior mobile-nav epic commit 9a77a73). Confirmed via `git show HEAD:app/src/components/Layout.tsx` that both `as="nav"` elements predate every edit made in this story — QrScanFab.tsx adds no `<nav>` element. Verify this pre-existing-and-unrelated characterization independently (e.g. `git log -p` on Layout.tsx / update-detection.spec.ts) and confirm it is routed to the backlog as a separate finding rather than silently left undiscovered — this story does not fix it (out of scope.includes; fixing it would mean either changing update-detection.spec.ts's selector or Layout.tsx's landmark semantics, neither part of S2's ACs).

A bonus (not required by S2's task brief, which only asked for the fast non-relay bucket) full-relay `make test-e2e` run was attempted after implementation to sanity-check Layout.tsx's shared-file blast radius: 180 passed cleanly (spanning groups admin/pairing/walled-garden/DM flows) before the run degraded into 46 failed / 19 skipped / 107 did-not-run over its 50.7-minute duration. Root-caused via log inspection: 41 of the 46 failures are `Error: page.goto: Page crashed` / `page.reload: Page crashed` thrown from the shared `bootUser` test helper on a bare `page.goto('/')` or `page.reload()` — i.e. the Chromium renderer tab itself crashing (host memory/resource exhaustion), not an application assertion failure, and every occurrence traces to the same generic boot helper rather than anything QR-scanner-specific. This matches this project's own documented chronic e2e-infra fragility (a memory note already on file records '~4 rotating ~30s VM-latency timeouts' and 'host fd-exhaustion (ENFILE) reads as a red unit suite' as known, unrelated host-capacity issues). Also confirmed and cleaned up: a stray `next dev` process left running on port 3000 from an earlier manual probe during this same implementation session was alive for the full 50-minute duration, adding avoidable memory/CPU pressure on the host throughout. Verify independently: (a) that the 'Page crashed' signature is indeed host-resource exhaustion and not something the QrScanFab/NpubQrScanner/Layout.tsx changes could plausibly trigger (e.g. a memory leak in the new component, a render loop) — inspect the ~180 tests that DID pass cleanly first, spanning many pages/routes that also render the now-globally-mounted QrScanFab, as evidence against a leak; (b) whether this run should be retried on a less contended host/at a time with more headroom before treating the full relay gate as confirmed, since this attempt is genuinely inconclusive (neither a clean pass nor an attributable regression) rather than either a pass or a fail.
